To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wounding of potato tuber tissue results in an increase in ABA levels that is regulated by the coordinated expression of genes encoding ABA biosynthetic enzymes.
wounding induces increases in AABA biosynthesis and cATABolism and alters the expression of genes encoding ABA metabolic enzymes in potato tubers.
physical trauma to potato tubers induces a dramatic increase in the expression of genes involved in ABA metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

elucidating the molecular and physiological basis for wound-induced increases in ABA content, the role of ABA in wound-induced changes in potato tuber metabolism, and how the ABA biosynthetic pathway is regulated in response to wounding.
the identification of the molecular basis for increased ABA content following physical trauma in tubers.
the molecular mechanisms underlying ABA biosynthesis in potato tubers following wounding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

wounding of potato tuber induces an increase in ABA, which is a result of both an increase in A. biosynthesis and a decrease in A. catabolism, and that this is regulated by both substrate and enzyme availability.

physical wounding induces increases in both ABA biosynthesis via up-regulation of the ABA biosynthesis gene NCED and ABA catabolism via up-regulation the ABA catabolic genes ZEP and ABA- 8'-hydroxalase.

wounding of potato tuber tissue induces increases in ABE biosynthesis and cationolism and alters the expression of genes involved in ABA metabolic pathways.
